60977-the-girl-scouts-at-singing-sands.title: The Girl Scouts At Singing Sands
60977-the-girl-scouts-at-singing-sands.creator: Unknown
60977-the-girl-scouts-at-singing-sands.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. “I’m afraid that by the time we’re snug down in our tents, it will be supper time,” the teacher replied, looking at her wrist watch. “Besides, we’re all rather tired after driving from Fairfield.”

arxiv-2104-04926.title: Deep learning-based Edge-aware pre and post-processing methods for JPEG compressed images
arxiv-2104-04926.creator: Dipti Mishra, Satish Kumar Singh, Rajat Kumar Singh
arxiv-2104-04926.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Dipti Mishra, Satish Kumar Singh, Rajat Kumar Singh. We propose a learning-based compression scheme that envelopes a standard codec between pre and post-processing deep CNNs. Specifically, we demonstrate improvements over prior approaches utilizing a compression-decompression network by introducing: (a) an edge-aware loss function to prevent blurring that is commonly occurred in prior works & (b) a super-resolution convolutional neural network (CNN) for post-processing along with a corresponding pre-processing network for improved rate-distortion performance in the low rate regime.

arxiv-2105-10544.title: Flow-driven spectral chaos (FSC) method for long-time integration of second-order stochastic dynamical systems Journal: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics (Elsevier)
arxiv-2105-10544.creator: Hugo Esquivel, Arun Prakash, Guang Lin
arxiv-2105-10544.description: Abstract For decades, uncertainty quantification techniques based on the spectral approach have been demonstrated to be computationally more efficient than the Monte Carlo method for a wide variety of problems, particularly when the dimensionality of the probability space is relatively low.

arxiv-2305-09175.title: Cooperative Aerial Transportation of Nonuniform Load through Quadrotors by Elastic and Flexible Cables
arxiv-2305-09175.creator: Ali Akbar Rezaei Lori, Mohammad Danesh, and Iman Izadi
arxiv-2305-09175.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Ali Akbar Rezaei Lori, Mohammad Danesh, and Iman Izadi. In this paper, first the full dynamics of aerial transportation of a rigid body with arbitrary number of quadrotors is derived. Then a control strategy is proposed to convey the nonuniform rigid body appropriately to the desired trajectory. In the dynamical model of this transportation system, not only the load is considered as a nonuniform and non-homogeneous rigid body but also mass, flexibility, and tension of the cables are considered.

arxiv-2308-11579.title: An alternative to SVM Method for Data Classification
arxiv-2308-11579.creator: Lakhdar Remaki Departement of Mathematics and Computer Science, Alfaisal University, KSA lremaki@bcamath.org
arxiv-2308-11579.description: Abstract Support vector machine (SVM), is a popular kernel method for data classification that demonstrated its efficiency for a large range of practical applications. The method suffers, however, from some weaknesses including; time processing, risk of failure of the optimization process for high dimension cases, generalization to multi-classes, unbalanced classes, and dynamic classification.

arxiv-2407-09655.title: Permutation Superposition Oracles for Quantum Query Lower Bounds
arxiv-2407-09655.creator: Christian Majenz, Giulio Malavolta, Michael Walter
arxiv-2407-09655.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Christian Majenz, Giulio Malavolta, Michael Walter. We propose a generalization of Zhandry’s compressed oracle method to random permutations, where an algorithm can query both the permutation and its inverse. We show how to use the resulting oracle simulation to bound the success probability of an algorithm for any predicate on input-output pairs, a key feature of Zhandry’s technique that had hitherto resisted attempts at generalization to random permutations.

arxiv-2410-11698.title: AI Rules? Characterizing Reddit Community Policies Towards AI-Generated Content
arxiv-2410-11698.creator: Travis Lloyd, Jennah Gosciak, Tung Nguyen, Mor Naaman
arxiv-2410-11698.description: Abstract . How are Reddit communities responding to AI-generated content? We explored this question through a large-scale analysis of subreddit community rules and their change over time. We collected the metadata and community rules for over 300,000 300,000 public subreddits and measured the prevalence of rules governing AI.

arxiv-2504-03611.title: On the small boundary property and 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -absorption, II
arxiv-2504-03611.creator: George A. Elliott, Zhuang Niu
arxiv-2504-03611.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by George A. Elliott, Zhuang Niu. Consider a minimal and free topological dynamical system ( X , ℤ d ) (X,\mathbb{Z}^{d}) . It is shown that zero mean dimension of ( X , ℤ d ) (X,\mathbb{Z}^{d}) is characterized by 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} -absorption of the crossed product C*-algebra A = C ⁡ ( X ) ⋊ ℤ d A=\mathrm{C}(X)\rtimes\mathbb{Z}^{d} , where 𝒵 \mathcal{Z} is the Jiang-Su algebra.

arxiv-2511-10279.title: PROPA: Toward Process-level Optimization in Visual Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2511-10279.creator: Yanbei Jiang, Chao Lei, Yihao Ding, Krista Ehinger, Jey Han Lau
arxiv-2511-10279.description: Abstract Despite significant progress, Vision-Language Models (VLMs) still struggle with complex visual reasoning, where multi-step dependencies cause early errors to cascade through the reasoning chain. Existing post-training paradigms are limited: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) relies on costly step-level annotations, while Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) methods like GRPO provide only sparse, outcome-level feedback, hindering stable optimization.

pmc-11322637.title: Efficient artificial intelligence-based assessment of the gastroesophageal valve with Hill classification through active learning
pmc-11322637.creator: Ioannis Kafetzis, Karl-Hermann Fuchs, Philipp Sodmann, Joel Troya, Wolfram Zoller, Alexander Meining, Alexander Hann
pmc-11322637.description: Standardized assessment of the gastroesophageal valve during endoscopy, attainable via the Hill classification, is important for clinical assessment and therapeutic decision making. The Hill classification is associated with the presence of hiatal hernia (HH), a common endoscopic finding connected to gastro-esophageal reflux disease. A novel efficient medical artificial intelligence (AI) training pipeline using active learning (AL) is designed.

pmc-11354140.title: Machine Learning for Patient-Based Real-Time Quality Control (PBRTQC), Analytical and Preanalytical Error Detection in Clinical Laboratory
pmc-11354140.creator: Nathan Lorde, Shivani Mahapatra, Tejas Kalaria, Jae-Ho Han
pmc-11354140.description: The rapidly evolving field of machine learning (ML), along with artificial intelligence in a broad sense, is revolutionising many areas of healthcare, including laboratory medicine. The amalgamation of the fields of ML and patient-based real-time quality control (PBRTQC) processes could improve the traditional PBRTQC and error detection algorithms in the laboratory.

pmc-11384435.title: Four-dimensional endocardial surface imaging with dynamic virtual reality rendering: a technical note
pmc-11384435.creator: Shi-Joon Yoo, Israel Valverde, Gregory S Perens, Kim-Lien Nguyen, J Paul Finn
pmc-11384435.description: Open heart surgery requires a proper understanding of the endocardial surface of the heart and vascular structures. While modern four-dimensional (4D) imaging enables excellent dynamic visualization of the blood pool, endocardial surface anatomy has not routinely been assessed. 4D image data were post-processed using commercially available virtual reality (VR) software.

pmc-11546127.title: Identification of aroma active compounds in Shanxi aged vinegar and tracing the source in the entire production process
pmc-11546127.creator: Jiao Wang, Ao Zhang, Yaao Zhou, Wenqing Zhang, Kai Liang, Juan-J. Román-Camacho, Jingli Zhou, Jia Song, Yu Zheng, Min Wang
pmc-11546127.description: The aroma-active compounds (AACs) of traditional vinegars are formed through complexed pathways. Moreover, their source is not clear yet. The composition of AACs throughout the entire process of Shanxi aged vinegar (SAV) production from the raw materials, alcohol fermentation (AF), acetic acid fermentation (AAF), fumigation and aging stages were analyzed.

pmc-12378941.title: Association between antidiabetic drug targets and psychiatric disorders
pmc-12378941.creator: Rui Yuan, Guorui Zhao, Zhe Lu, Yunqing Zhu, Zhewei Kang, Yuyanan Zhang, Yaoyao Sun, Yang Yang, Yundan Liao, Xiaoyang Feng, Junyuan Sun, Jing Guo, Weihua Yue
pmc-12378941.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Psychiatric disorders present a significant global health burden with limited effective medications. Observing the widespread comorbidities between diabetes and psychiatric disorders, we explored the potential of repurposing antidiabetic drug targets for psychiatric treatments. We identified 32 target genes of 60 antidiabetics and performed Mendelian randomization analyses using expression and protein quantitative trait loci data from brain tissues alongside summary data for seven psychiatric disorders.

pmc-12546854.title: Assessment of macroscopic properties of ecological building materials based on chemical microscopic phase composition and interface interaction mechanisms
pmc-12546854.creator: Yan Pang
pmc-12546854.description: This study investigates the macroscopic properties of ecological building materials prepared from recycled industrial waste through comprehensive analysis of chemical microscopic phase composition and interface interaction mechanisms. Three primary industrial wastes (fly ash, blast furnace slag, and steel slag) were systematically incorporated as cement replacements at various proportions.

pmc-12604826.title: Leveraging Social Media and Crowdsourcing to Recruit and Retain Military Veterans With Posttraumatic Stress Disorder or Experience of Harmful Gambling for mHealth Interventions: Descriptive Study
pmc-12604826.creator: Conor Heath, Jess M Williams, Daniel Leightley, Dominic Murphy, Simon Dymond, Lorraine Buis
pmc-12604826.description: BackgroundMilitary veterans may be at increased risk of posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) compared to the general population. PTSD is often comorbid with harmful and problematic patterns of gambling. Behavioral therapies such as acceptance and commitment therapy have shown promise in treating these co-occurring disorders, especially if combined with mobile health (mHealth) interventions to circumvent known help-seeking barriers faced by veterans.

pmc-12639747.title: Effects of canagliflozin combined with metformin therapy on insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus
pmc-12639747.creator: Yimin Shu, Xiaoyu Chen, Pingfeng Wang
pmc-12639747.description: ObjectiveTo investigate the effects of canagliflozin combined with metformin on insulin sensitivity in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).MethodsPatients with T2DM who were treated in the outpatient department of the hospital between May 2023 and May 2024 were selected.

pmc-12820196.title: Tractable mouse TNBC models capture the heterogeneous tumor immune microenvironment and adaptation to PD-L1 blockade
pmc-12820196.creator: Robbe Salembier, Caro De Haes, Kristel Demeyere, Steven Van Laere, Lucie Cervenkova, Nicolaas Van Renne, Christos Sotiriou, Evelyne Meyer, Jonas Steenbrugge
pmc-12820196.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) patients exhibit variable responses to programmed death (PD)-ligand (L)1 blockade, largely determined by the ‘hot’ vs ‘cold’ state of the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME). We here characterized nine mouse TNBC models, relying on intraductal mammary gland inoculation of established mouse TNBC cell lines, with a heterogeneous TIME to study anti-PD-L1 resistance mechanisms.

pmc-12973159.title: Emotional challenges in neurodivergent children and young people: Progress and open questions for research and practice
pmc-12973159.creator: Giorgia Michelini, Alessio Bellato
pmc-12973159.description: This Editorial introduces the March 2026 issue of JCPP Advances, marking the journal's sixth year with 15 impactful articles spanning key topics in child and adolescent mental health. A recurring theme across several articles is the investigation of emotional challenges—encompassing depression, anxiety, and self‐harm—particularly in the context of neurodivergence.

pmc-13357059.title: Survival improvement and widening social disadvantage-related disparities in osteosarcoma: a Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-based retrospective cohort study
pmc-13357059.creator: Shilin Luo, Chuang Li, Leilei Tian, Rui Shi, Yi Luo
pmc-13357059.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundEvidence on contemporary survival trends and social disadvantage-related disparities in osteosarcoma remains limited due to its rarity. According to the theory of fundamental causes, socially advantaged populations may benefit more from medical progress, potentially widening survival disparities over time.

pmc-13436918.title: Physician-assigned Diagnosis Versus Questionnaire-based Measures in Individuals with Nociceptive, Neuropathic, and Nociplastic Pain: A Mechanism-based Characterization of Chronic Pain Patients
pmc-13436918.creator: Netanel Kamel, Tseela Hoffman, May Haddad, Amir Minerbi
pmc-13436918.description: BackgroundThe International Association for the Study of Pain (IASP) has defined three mechanisms for chronic pain: nociceptive, neuropathic, and nociplastic. Accurate differentiation between these mechanisms is essential for treatment selection but remains challenging due to symptom overlap and reliance on clinical judgment. Patient-reported questionnaires may support diagnosis, though their diagnostic accuracy relative to physician assessment has not been fully established.
